name: baseray API
description:
The baseray API gives programmatic read access to baseray's building catalogue for Romania and Czechia: each building's footprint, height, volume, floor area, floors, category, address and postcode, flood zone and seismic risk, what its record states (such as its construction year), rooftop solar potential, whether solar panels are already on the roof, and the businesses whose registered office is at its address.

## Authentication
Every endpoint except this document and the public building pages needs a workspace API key, sent as a bearer token:

    Authorization: Bearer br_live_…

Create keys in the baseray app under **Settings → API keys**. A key is shown once, when it is created; store it as a secret. A key stops working when it is revoked, when it expires, or when the person who created it leaves the workspace. Cookies, sessions and other tokens are not accepted.

## Rate limits and quotas
Each key may make 60 requests a minute, and all of a workspace's keys together 5,000 requests a UTC day. Every authenticated response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the minute window resets) for the key, and `X-Daily-Quota-Limit` and `X-Daily-Quota-Remaining` for the workspace. Past a limit the API answers `429` with `rate_limited` or `quota_exceeded` and a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

## Public building pages
The endpoints under `/public` serve the facts behind baseray's public pages and need no key. They answer the same to everyone and may be cached as their `Cache-Control` says. Each client address may make 120 requests a minute; past that they answer `429` with a `Retry-After` header. Their field names are camelCase, every fact is its value or `null` (unknown) with `estimate` saying whether it is modelled, and their errors are `{"error": "not_found"}`, `{"error": "invalid_parameter", "message": "..."}`, `{"error": "rate_limited"}` or `{"error": "unavailable"}`.

## Errors
Every non-2xx response outside `/public` has the same body: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "parameter": "..."}}`. `code` is stable and machine-readable; `message` is for people; `parameter` names the query or path parameter at fault for `invalid_parameter`. Unknown query parameters are refused rather than ignored.

## Pagination
`GET /buildings` returns one ranked page: `meta.total` counts every match (up to 10,000; `meta.total_is_capped` is true when counting stopped there), and `links.next` is the URL of the next page, or null on the last one. `offset + limit` may not exceed 10,000; to reach further, narrow the area.

## Values
Field names are snake_case (camelCase under `/public`), lengths in metres, areas in m², volumes in m³, dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, timestamps ISO 8601 UTC. A value baseray has no record of is `null`, meaning unknown, never zero. An address is given only as a record states it, and `address_evidence` says whether that is an address record of the building or a listing of a business at it: the road nearest a building no address names is `nearest_road`, never `address`. A figure's `basis` says what it rests on: `measured` (the building itself was measured), `stated` (a record states it for the building) or `estimated` (modelled, not measured). A business registered at an address is never evidence that it owns or occupies the building.

**Credits.** Every building an answer returns costs the workspace 1 credit, once: a building it opened (in the app, the API or an assistant) in the last 365 days is free. A page of results is charged all or nothing; when the workspace has too few credits left this month the request answers `402 insufficient_credits` and returns nothing. `X-Credits-Charged` and `X-Credits-Remaining` say what a request cost and what is left.
